items.title: UK pensions department hit by ‘serious cyber incident’, minister says – UK politics live
items.desc: Pat McFadden says the government doesn’t believe any personal data has been compromised Tell us: have you been affected by the DWP ‘cyber incident’ According to Downdetector , which tracks online service outages, reports of problems with the government website appeared to begin last night and peaked at about 8am this morning. Tory MP Neil Shastri-Hurst has also commented on the disruption at the DWP, saying the incident highlights the importance of protecting essential public services and ensuring they can recover quickly when systems fail. Today’s cyber incident at DWP is a stark reminder that national resilience is not a tomorrow issue. It means protecting the essential services people rely on every day, with secure systems and the ability to recover quickly when things go wrong.” Continue reading...

items.title: ‘Punched in the guts’: Poundland staff left reeling as it goes into administration
items.desc: Workers are sad but unsurprised as closures and job losses loom, while 2,000 suppliers will take a big hit Poundland staff fear they’ll be left out in the cold for Christmas. When will workers have a say in their future? “I feel Gordon Brothers punched us in the guts and took us down,” says Kelvin Blake, one of thousands of Poundland workers at risk of redundancy after the budget retailer’s US-based owners rejected at least two solvent bids for it. While administrators at AlixPartners, who were appointed on Wednesday, continue to consider bids for the whole group, which has 600 stores in the UK and Ireland including the Dealz chain, more than 10,000 staff and thousands of suppliers face a grim Christmas of uncertainty. Continue reading...

items.title: UK’s taste for cow’s milk sours as sales hit record low
items.desc: Environmental and animal welfare concerns, and taste preferences, are behind rising popularity of vegan alternatives Has milk gotta lotta bottle? It may not have as much as it used to, with official data showing Britons are buying less cow’s milk than at any point since records began. Guardian analysis of the government’s family food survey shows the average person bought 1.8 pints (1,024ml) of cow’s milk a week in 2024-25 – the lowest level in the record’s 52-year history and less than half the amount of milk bought in 1974. items.title: Oxford museum displays seized belongings of Naga freedom fighter Gaidinliu for first time
items.desc: Notebooks, clothes and ritual objects taken by British forces in India in the 1930s go on show at Pitt Rivers Museum In 1932, British forces in north-east India imprisoned a 17-year-old girl called Gaidinliu for leading an uprising against colonial rule. While pursuing the freedom fighter through hills and valleys in the homeland of the Naga people, colonial officers also seized some of her most treasured possessions. They were sent to the University of Oxford’s Pitt Rivers Museum and kept in storage. Now, for the first time, the museum is exhibiting the collection of 27 items, including a basket of Gaidinliu’s notebooks believed to contain her prophetic visions as the leader of a Naga Indigenous religion, clothes, bracelets and amulets. Continue reading...

items.title: What we learned from the government’s latest release of Mandelson documents
items.desc: From attempted influence on Starmer’s 2025 reshuffle to refusing to sell shares in a lobbying firm, here are some of the key points UK politics live – latest updates The government has published 32 new documents about Peter Mandelson’s appointment and tenure as British ambassador to Washington. This is the third tranche of papers since a parliamentary motion, known as a humble address, in February 2026 for “all papers” relevant to be released. Some material was withheld by the Metropolitan police from earlier releases in March and June on the basis it could prejudice an ongoing investigation into Mandelson. A number of files continue to be withheld but earlier this month the force informed the government that various records could now be disclosed. Continue reading...

items.title: Rosebank rebellion: are resignations next? – podcast
items.desc: Close to 100 Labour MPs have sent a letter to Andy Burnham calling for him to reject the Rosebank oilfield licence.
